title.narrative: Transforming Andhra Pradesh aquaculture to a sustainable, reduced footprint and climate resilient food system

description.narrative: Fisheries and Aquaculture comprise an important sector of food production in India, contributing sizably to the food basket. In India, this promising “sunrise” sector provides livelihood, employment, and entrepreneurship to more than 28 million fishers and fish farmers at the primary level and several lakhs along the value chain. India is the third largest fish producing country in the world with a production of 18.4 million tonnes in 2023-24, contributing ~8 percent to the global fish production and ranks second in aquaculture production. Fish and fishery products have recently emerged as one of the largest groups in agricultural exports of India, with an all-time high achievement in marine products exports with 17,81,602 MT worth USD 7,203 million (INR 605,240 million) in the year 2023-2024. While fishing and fish farming are important sources of employment, the bulk of employment is in the post-harvest subsector, in areas such as fish processing and marketing. For each person employed in capture fisheries and aquaculture primary production, about three to four related jobs are produced in secondary activities (e.g. fish processing, trade, and marketing). Also, the value chain players in aquaculture like hatcheries, feed mills and input manufacturers and suppliers have much employment Assuming that on average each jobholder provides for three dependents or family members, it is estimated that overall, fisheries and aquaculture contributes to the livelihoods of 10–12 percent of the world’s population. Fisheries and aquaculture also generate pre-harvest jobs such as boatbuilding and maintenance; engine and gear manufacturing; and provision of support services in harbours, at landing sites, and in dry docks and repair and maintenance workshops. This employment does not account for as many jobs as in post-harvest, but it still constitutes a considerable workforce. The Livelihoods Enhancement and Diversification (LED) approach needs to be taken up as a priority. Moving away from the casual and ad hoc skill development training, a comprehensive approach to build up from the stakeholder interest and market demand, ensuring the complete forward and backward linkages need to be put in place. The small-scale farmers who are resource poor need special attention in an inclusive approach in fisheries development. The FAO Voluntary Guidelines for Securing Sustainable Small-scale Fisheries in the Context of Food Security and Poverty Eradication (FAO, 2015)14 is a guide in this regard. Following the four pillars of decent rural employment, the project will: Pillar 1 (Employment creation and enterprise development)Invest in sustainable and inclusive value chain development, with a particular focus on small-scale fish workers. It will also improve the access of small-scale fish workers, including women and youth, to productive resources and alternative income strategies. Through knowledge management, the project will invest in relevant knowledge and statistical systems for collecting, analysing, and disseminating more comprehensive and reliable employment data relevant for decision making in fisheries and aquaculture. The project will also foster policy coherence across sectors.Pillar 2 (Social protection)Strengthen policy measures for extension of social protection to include both formal and informal fish workers, including national citizens and migrants, as also support the improvement and implementation of occupational safety and health measures (OSH) in fisheries and aquaculture based on participatory assessment of OSH needs. Pillar 3 (Standards and rights at work)Strengthen the implementation of available legal and policy instruments to support decent work standards and particularly address conditions of fish workers in local processing units supplying domestic markets. Pillar 4 (Governance and social dialogue)Strengthen collective fisheries, aquaculture, and fish workers’ organizations, with enhanced leadership roles for women and youth.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To support the integrated management of terrestrial/aquatic landscapes in Andhra Pradesh through sustainable, intensified, and reduced footprint aquaculture production systems; that reduce environmental degradation at the production level and throughout the value chain, sustainably increase production and climate resilience, enhance producersâ€™ incomes and resilience, reduce risks and meet global needs for healthy, affordable food in an equitable manner following ecosystem approach to aquaculture.
